name: Skyhook

modes.label: Native service
modes.note: Hardware and complete resource tariff unverified.

plans.name: Free BYOC
plans.note: No payment method required. Up to 3 Git-connected users, 3 services, 1 cluster. Self-onboarding. Your own cloud bill is separate.

plans.name: Premium monthly BYOC
plans.note: $1k/month billed monthly; up to 10 Git-connected users, 15 services, 5 clusters; professional onboarding; 24/5 support. Flat fee, not usage credit; infrastructure paid directly to the cloud provider.

plans.name: Premium yearly BYOC
plans.note: Yearly toggle '-20%': $800/month billed annually (annual commitment). Same limits as Premium monthly.

caveats: Free own-cloud 3 git users/3 services/1 cluster; Premium $1000/month up to 10 users/15 services/5 clusters, annual 20% off; Enterprise custom. Infrastructure cost is separate. YC mentions optional fully hosted cluster, but no specific host tariff verified.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Cloud charges are never included: Skyhook runs only on the customer's AWS/GCP/Azure/OCI/on-prem Kubernetes. Existing cloud credits apply. No hosted-cluster option is offered on the live site (the older YC listing's 'fully hosted cluster' is not reflected).

fleet.verification: Free platform account requires no payment method; customer cloud billing separate.
fleet.tiers: Free: 1 cluster/3 services. Premium: 5 clusters/15 services. Enterprise: custom/unlimited advertised.
fleet.notes: BYOC orchestration plan limits are not machine counts. Underlying cloud quotas and verification determine new-customer fleet feasibility.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

harness_api.quote: The Skyhook ChatOps Assistant is available in the context of a specific Service. You can find the assistant in the "ChatOps" tab of any of your services.
harness_api.note: Skyhook's own 'Skyhook Agent'/ChatOps assistant is a UI chat for infra that acts via GitHub PRs; not an agent harness running inside a sandbox, and no API to drive it. The AI-ready page points to external MCP servers (Radar OSS) for agents to read cluster state.

ingress_rules.quote: Ingress — enable ingress, ingress host, ingress class
ingress_rules.note: Per service/environment you choose whether to expose it via Ingress (nginx) or Gateway API HTTPRoute, host and class; otherwise services stay cluster-internal. No first-party IP allowlist or authenticated-URL feature documented (could be done with nginx annotations/Envoy in the customer's cluster).

secret_proxy.quote: The Sealed Secrets controller in your Kubernetes cluster decrypts secrets at runtime using a private key
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are Bitnami Sealed Secrets in Git, decrypted into Kubernetes Secrets and injected into pods as env vars; no credential-injecting proxy.

isolation.quote: Secure Separation: Each service runs in its own isolated environment with enforced CPU, memory, and network limits using Kubernetes security best practices.
isolation.note: Skyhook deploys application containers onto the customer's own Kubernetes cluster (shared kernel per node); it is not a VM/microVM product.

image_oci.quote: Select an Image ... Choose the container image you want. Skyhook supports images from public or private registries, giving you full flexibility.
image_oci.note: Build page confirms output is an OCI-compliant container image.

docker_inside.quote: Skyhook creates Kubernetes resources on the cluster. Kubernetes schedules your pods on available nodes, optimizing resource usage.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Skyhook runs your pre-built OCI image as a standard Kubernetes pod (containerd runtime); no documented docker-in-docker/privileged mode.

nested_virt.quote: Skyhook creates Kubernetes resources on the cluster. Kubernetes schedules your pods on available nodes, optimizing resource usage.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Standard Kubernetes pods on the customer's cluster; no /dev/kvm access documented.

desktop.quote: Skyhook is all the automation and work you would do to deliver a kubernetes-based platform, available immediately, right in your cloud, on your terms, together with a developer interface.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Skyhook is a Kubernetes application deployment/IDP platform, not a desktop/VNC product.

browser.quote: Skyhook is all the automation and work you would do to deliver a kubernetes-based platform, available immediately, right in your cloud, on your terms, together with a developer interface.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

computer_use.quote: Skyhook is all the automation and work you would do to deliver a kubernetes-based platform, available immediately, right in your cloud, on your terms, together with a developer interface.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.quote: Skyhook is all the automation and work you would do to deliver a kubernetes-based platform, available immediately, right in your cloud, on your terms, together with a developer interface.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

captcha_solving.quote: Skyhook is all the automation and work you would do to deliver a kubernetes-based platform, available immediately, right in your cloud, on your terms, together with a developer interface.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

ssh.quote: Execute a command in a running pod. Opens an interactive shell by default. Uses your current kubectl context.
ssh.note: Provides shell access via `skyhook exec` (a kubectl-exec wrapper), not SSH protocol access to a machine.

snapshot.quote: If a container crashes or a node goes offline, it will restart or reschedule automatically.
snapshot.note: No disk/memory snapshot or checkpoint feature documented; recovery is via Kubernetes self-healing/rescheduling, not stateful snapshots.

snapshot_auto.quote: If a container crashes or a node goes offline, it will restart or reschedule automatically.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: If a container crashes or a node goes offline, it will restart or reschedule automatically.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No API/CLI snapshot command documented (CLI reference has no snapshot/checkpoint verb).

fork.quote: Manage deployment environments at the organization level — cluster, namespace, labels, clone-from-source, AutoDeploy, and per-workload env name prefixes.
fork.note: 'Clone-from-source' creates a fresh environment from config/source, not a fork of a running machine's live state.

fork_running.quote: Manage deployment environments at the organization level — cluster, namespace, labels, clone-from-source, AutoDeploy, and per-workload env name prefixes.
fork_running.note: No feature to clone a live running instance without redeploying/restarting it.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Manage deployment environments at the organization level — cluster, namespace, labels, clone-from-source, AutoDeploy, and per-workload env name prefixes.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No memory-state cloning feature; new environments are fresh pod starts.

pause_resume.quote: KEDA also supports scale-to-zero — you can set minimum replicas to 0 and the workload will spin down completely when idle, then spin back up when the first event arrives.
pause_resume.note: Scaling a workload to zero replicas via KEDA stops compute billing for that workload and it resumes automatically on the next event; not a distinct manual pause/resume API.

wake_on_request.quote: KEDA also supports scale-to-zero — you can set minimum replicas to 0 and the workload will spin down completely when idle, then spin back up when the first event arrives.

auto_stop_idle.quote: KEDA also supports scale-to-zero — you can set minimum replicas to 0 and the workload will spin down completely when idle

live_resize.quote: InPlaceOrRecreate: Update in-place when possible, fall back to recreate otherwise. Requires a Kubernetes version that supports in-place pod resize.
live_resize.note: VPA can adjust CPU/memory of running pods in-place on clusters that support it; falls back to recreate otherwise.

agent_harnesses.quote: Skyhook is all the automation and work you would do to deliver a kubernetes-based platform, available immediately, right in your cloud, on your terms, together with a developer interface.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Skyhook is a DevOps/deployment platform; it does not offer preinstalled coding-agent harnesses.

own_agent_api.quote: Skyhook's agent provides developers and devops with the data they need. It's an agent that already knows your entire environment.
own_agent_api.note: Skyhook's own AI agent (ChatOps assistant) is a chat UI for infra Q&A/actions inside a service's 'ChatOps' tab; no documented first-party API to drive it programmatically.

mcp_server.quote: Pair with Radar's MCP server for Kubernetes to let agents read cluster state safely.
mcp_server.note: Skyhook points agents to Radar (a separate OSS sister project) for an MCP server; Skyhook itself does not ship its own MCP server.

lang_python.quote: Multi-Language Support: Build applications in Node, Python, Java, Go, or any language. If it can run in a container, Skyhook can build it.

lang_node.quote: Multi-Language Support: Build applications in Node, Python, Java, Go, or any language. If it can run in a container, Skyhook can build it.

public_ipv4.quote: Once running, your service is reachable via a stable endpoint. Skyhook can provision a DNS name and TLS certificate for public services.
public_ipv4.note: Public reachability is via DNS name + TLS (Ingress/Gateway API), not a documented dedicated public IPv4 per machine.

inbound_https.quote: Once running, your service is reachable via a stable endpoint. Skyhook can provision a DNS name and TLS certificate for public services.

guest_firewall.quote: Secure Separation: Each service runs in its own isolated environment with enforced CPU, memory, and network limits using Kubernetes security best practices.
guest_firewall.note: Skyhook workloads are standard (non-root, non-privileged) Kubernetes pods, not a VM/microVM with guest-level root; not applicable.

windows.quote: Build applications in Node, Python, Java, Go, or any language. If it can run in a container, Skyhook can build it.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. All examples, CLI, and docs describe Linux container/Kubernetes workflows; no Windows container/Windows Server node support mentioned.

macos.quote: Skyhook is all the automation and work you would do to deliver a kubernetes-based platform, available immediately, right in your cloud, on your terms, together with a developer interface.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Kubernetes-based container deployment platform; no macOS machines.

arm64.quote: NodePool covers the required instance types — if your pod requests a specific architecture (arm64) or a large resource footprint, make sure the NodePool's instance family selection includes nodes that can satisfy it.

self_host.quote: Bring your own GKE, EKS, AKS, or any Kubernetes-compatible cluster. Skyhook installs a lightweight read-only connector via Helm — clusters stay in your account.
self_host.note: Skyhook is a hosted SaaS control plane you log into (skyhook.io); you connect your own cluster to it, but you cannot run the Skyhook control plane itself on your own infrastructure per the documented model.

open_source.quote: Resources ... Changelog Status Trust Center Radar (OSS)
open_source.note: Skyhook's own footer distinguishes 'Radar (OSS)' as the open-source sister project; the core Skyhook platform itself is not labeled or documented as open source.

eu_data_residency.quote: We support AWS, GCP, Azure, and OCI, as well as on-prem and bring-your-own Kubernetes clusters. Deploy wherever your workloads live.
eu_data_residency.note: Because workloads run on the customer's own cloud cluster (BYOC), the customer can choose EU regions for the actual machines/data; Skyhook's own control-plane subprocessors (Trust Center) are US-based.

max_session_h.quote: Deployments spread across multiple nodes for resilience. Your app instances remain available even during node maintenance or outages.
max_session_h.note: Services are long-running Kubernetes deployments meant to run continuously (not a bounded sandbox session); they run until stopped/scaled down by the user.

egress_ip_type.quote: A Kubernetes platform that generates the workflows, manifests, and GitOps plumbing — you keep the repo and the cloud account.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: Skyhook is BYOC — workloads run inside the customer's own AWS/GCP/Azure Kubernetes cluster, so outbound traffic egresses through that cloud provider's normal datacenter IP ranges, not a residential/mobile pool. No Skyhook-managed egress IP feature is documented.

persistent_disk.quote: Storage Classes — Lists available storage backends for persistent volumes (e.g., standard-rwo, premium-rwo on GCP; gp2, gp3 on AWS). The default storage class is marked; that's what PVCs use when you don't specify storageClassName.
persistent_disk.note: derived: full Kubernetes clusters with native PersistentVolume/PersistentVolumeClaim support (also listed as a browsable resource kind in the Resource Viewer), so data on a PVC-backed StatefulSet/pod survives restarts.

volume_attach.note: Skyhook's cluster Resource Viewer natively tracks PersistentVolumeClaim/StorageClass objects and the cluster view page explains provisioning volumes via storage classes, i.e. extra persistent volumes can be attached (standard Kubernetes PVCs) to workloads deployed through Skyhook.

volume_shared.quote: Lists available storage backends for persistent volumes (e.g., standard-rwo, premium-rwo on GCP; gp2, gp3 on AWS).
volume_shared.note: not offered: the only storage classes Skyhook's own docs name are *-rwo (ReadWriteOnce, single-mounter) classes; no ReadWriteMany/shared-volume feature or storage class is documented.

egress_allowlist.quote: Networking — Service, Ingress, NetworkPolicy, Gateway, HTTPRoute ... Toggle from Resources to Traffic to see the network flow between workloads, based on real-time service mesh or NetworkPolicy data.
egress_allowlist.note: derived: full Kubernetes clusters natively support NetworkPolicy egress rules, and Skyhook's Resource Viewer/Traffic view surfaces NetworkPolicy objects and traffic; rules are authored as standard K8s manifests via Skyhook's GitOps flow rather than a dedicated allowlist UI.

egress_http_rules.quote: Networking — Service, Ingress, NetworkPolicy, Gateway, HTTPRoute
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: the documented egress control primitive is Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, which operates at L3/L4 (IP/port); no HTTP method/path-level egress rule feature is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: The connector runs as a pod in your cluster and communicates outbound to the Skyhook API. No inbound ports or public endpoints are required.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Skyhook is a BYOC control plane over the customer's own cluster/VPC; it documents its own connector's outbound calls but offers no feature to assign or manage a fixed outbound IP for customer workloads — that would be configured at the cloud provider (NAT gateway) level, not through Skyhook.

gpu.note: Skyhook's Jobs/Argo Workflows docs show first-party support for requesting GPU resources per step, plus nodeSelector/affinity examples for scheduling onto GPU node pools (e.g. g4dn.xlarge); Jobs overview also lists GPU as a customizable per-environment resource allocation.

hipaa.note: Skyhook's Trust Center lists only SOC 2 (Type II report available) under Compliance; no HIPAA/BAA program is mentioned anywhere in the docs or trust pages.

usage_api.quote: Infrastructure cost is separate. Skyhook runs only on the customer's AWS/GCP/Azure/OCI/on-prem Kubernetes. Existing cloud credits apply.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; Skyhook is a BYOC (Bring Your Own Cloud) platform with no hosted infrastructure. Platform charges are flat-fee ($1000/month Premium, $800/month annually). Billable compute (vCPU, RAM, storage) is metered by the customer's cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure/OCI), not by Skyhook. Skyhook provides no API to query usage/cost of individual services or workloads; that is the responsibility of the underlying cloud provider's billing APIs (AWS Cost Explorer, GCP Billing Export, Azure Cost Management, etc.).
